title: Adaptive stream sink quarantine and progressive output compaction for abrupt client failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Abrupt client disconnects during streaming generations (including function/tool calls and structured output) create trade-offs: immediate garbage collection reduces storage/metadata pressure but loses partial useful output; keeping state indefinitely raises memory and KV cache pressure and increases SLO exposure. Current heuristics either aggressively GC or keep long TTLs which cause tail latency regressions during spikes.

Proposal: implement an adaptive "stream sink quarantine" with progressive output compaction. Key ideas:
- Quarantine window: when a client disconnect is detected (socket close/heartbeat gap), mark the generation's sink state as QUARANTINED rather than immediately deleted. Quarantine initial window is short (configurable base, e.g., 20s) and extends adaptively based on heuristics.
- Heuristic-driven extension: extend quarantine when recent traffic shows high resume attempts, when the generation contains tool/function calls that produced idempotent side-effects, or when the session had >X structured-output tokens. Decrease extension if system is under memory/kv pressure.
- Progressive compaction: during quarantine we compact stored partial outputs incrementally: first remove ephemeral streaming bufffers and per-client retransmit queues, then compact token buffers into a compacted prefix snapshot (N tokens preserved), then optionally checkpoint minimal resume metadata to an object store and release hot memory/KV entries.
- Function/tool-call safety: for streams with in-flight tool invocations, ensure a small durable receipt record is kept to avoid duplicate tool execution on resume. Design a lightweight idempotency token persisted to object store and referenced from compacted state.
- Compatibility/SDK shim: introduce X-Stream-Resume-TTL header and a backward-compatible resume_token format version. SDKs prior to resume-v2 will get shortened TTLs and a compatibility flag so server-side resume attempts degrade gracefully.
- Flow-control integration: when quarantine compaction begins, update adaptive batching and prefix-cache heuristics so other concurrent generations can claim memory. Emit backpressure signals to routing layer to avoid new long-lived streams on saturated nodes.

Goals: reclaim memory and KV capacity more quickly without losing high-value resumable states; minimize duplicate tool calls; preserve UX for typical reconnections; prevent quarantine from causing latency regressions.

Success metrics (examples):
- Percent reduction in hot-KV entries per abrupt-disconnect event (target: 60% median reduction within 60s)
- Resume success rate within 2 minutes after disconnect (target: >= 95% for resumable-compliant SDKs)
- Number of duplicate tool invocations attributed to resume logic (target: < 0.1% of resumed sessions)
- P95 serving latency during GC events compared to baseline (target: < 10% regression)

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged server-side implementation + unit/integration tests (internal canary)
2) Enable for internal traffic only for 1 week; collect metrics and validate non-duplication for tool-calls
3) Gradual customer ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for resume-v2 SDKs; compatibility mode for older SDKs off by default
4) Full on for all traffic once metrics stable and no regression observed over 48h

Implementation notes:
- New state machine states: ACTIVE -> QUARANTINED -> COMPACTED -> ARCHIVED/GC
- Compaction steps implemented as idempotent jobs; each step emits an event for observability and can be retried
- Use object store (S3/GCS) for long-duration resume checkpoints; KV/Redis used for hot resume metadata only
- Add a configurable controller that monitors node memory/KV pressure and reduces quarantine TTLs globally during sustained pressure

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk of duplicate tool execution if idempotency tokens are not enforced by tool integrations; mitigation: require tool-call receipts for resumable streams or convert tool-calls to at-least-once with dedupe layer when possible
- Additional operational complexity: new states and compaction jobs increase surface area for bugs; mitigation: gated rollout and strong SLO-based alerts
- Possible resume UX degradation for very old SDKs; mitigation: compatibility defaults preserve basic resume but shorter TTLs and docs for upgrade path

Docs and migration:
- Add Console page and runtime docs describing X-Stream-Resume-TTL and resume-v2
- SDK patches to expose resume tokens and correctly set compatibility flags
- Migration guide for customers with long-lived streams or legacy SDKs

2026-03-03: Prototype server-side compaction job implemented; local tests show 55% reduction in hot-KV entries for synthetic workload.

2026-03-07: Integration tests added for resume-v2 token validation and tool-call dedupe; found edge case where long-running tool invocations blocked compaction - added short-lived lease for in-flight tool records.
2026-03-10: Feature flag toggles and canary plan approved. Preparing internal canary deployment next week.
